name: cnsplots
summary: Publication-quality scientific figures in Python via the cnsplots package, including the rcParams style contract, grid/multi-panel composition patterns, dense journal-figure techniques, and cross-panel color strategy.

verification.method: mamba env with cnsplots 0.7.0; ran the vendored upstream showcase figure1.py and figure2.py standalone and confirmed both produce their SVG; audited every color decision in that source and measured the color each palette assigns to a shared category, plus per-palette greyscale luma separation; traced the draw_event/_on_draw relayout mechanism and confirmed it is connected automatically by panel(), is multipanel-only, is triggered by savefig, and that fig.tight_layout() is a measured no-op on multipanel figures; ran all four bundled scripts; ran all four templates and rendered each to PNG for visual inspection; measured the rcParams before/after diff and every settings value rather than transcribing them; empirically tested multipanel panel alignment, below= stacking, GridSpec-in-panel durability across savefig, and the inset_axes alternative. Also reproduced the upstream showcase Figure 1 and Figure 2 end to end and inspected both renders, then verified the showcase-only techniques independently: negative pad_left offsets, composite plotter internal axes, upsetplot ax= overflow, whether cns.utils._capture_detached_axes_layout is load-bearing, and the full set of names cns.palettes() accepts.
verification.notes: Figure density was tuned against a measured metric (fraction of interior all-empty pixel rows): upstream Figure 1 is 4.77 percent and Figure 2 is 5.44 percent, and templates/dense_figure.py now sits at 4.22 percent, down from 7.96 percent before below= interlocking was added. mutool absent in this environment, so SVG export falls back to plain matplotlib SVG with a RuntimeWarning; unrelated to skill correctness. Reproducing the upstream showcase surfaced overlapping heatmap legends in its Figure 1 panel R at this font/size, which is why the legend_* nudges are documented as size-specific and requiring re-tuning.
